statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if there exists an index j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that deleting the element at position j from nums gives a strictly increasing sequence. Deleting position j from a sequence of length n gives the sequence of length n-1 whose k-th element, for 0 <= k < n-1, is nums[k] when k < j and nums[k+1] when k >= j; this deleted sequence is strictly increasing when for every k with 0 <= k < len(nums)-2, its k-th element is less than its (k+1)-th element. If no such j exists, r = false.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on nums and r' the result of the function on nums'. Then both calls return results and r = r'.
preconditions: 2 <= len(nums) <= 1000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000, and nums' is any slice with len(nums') = len(nums), 1 <= nums'[i] <= 1000 for every 0 <= i < len(nums'), and for every i,k with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= k < len(nums), nums[i] < nums[k] if and only if nums'[i] < nums'[k].
